Definition: , including nominative masculine plural οὗτοι, nominative feminine singular αὕτη, and nominative feminine plural αὕται from the article G3588 and G846; the he (she or it), i.e. this or that (often with article repeated):--he (it was that), hereof, it, she, such as, the same, these, they, this (man, same, woman), which, who.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, hoûtos is the word for this, these, he, she, it. In Matthew 1:20, the text says "But while he thought on these things."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, hoûtos means this, these, he, she, it, and I leave it at that.
RelatedTopics: Word of God; Faith; Christian Life
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; The Angel Appears to Joseph; Jesus Heals a Demoniac in the Capernaum Synagogue
